title: SDK Client Evolution: Language Support Gap Analysis & Streaming Ergonomics Triage
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Produce a prioritized intake and execution plan for SDK and client-library requests from enterprise customers and internal partners. Focus areas: (1) language support gaps for enterprise-critical languages, (2) standardizing auth patterns (rotating tokens, SSO/SSO delegation, service accounts), and (3) streaming ergonomics (resumable streams, backpressure, byte-level framing, connection recovery).

Scope and goals:
- Triage inbound requests collected via support, sales, and Solutions Engineering into a ranked backlog with clear acceptance criteria.
- Define a reproducible prioritization rubric that balances customer ROI, integration complexity, maintenance cost, and platform constraints.
- Produce SDK API patterns for streaming that are ergonomically consistent across languages (Python, Node, Java, Go, .NET, Rust) and reduce common footguns (token expiry mid-stream, partial-response handling, reconnect semantics).
- Specify auth primitives and a recommended pattern library: short-lived token hooks, automatic token refresh callback, built-in example for SSO with redirect flow for web SDKs, service-account signing for server-to-server.
- Deliverables: prioritization matrix (CSV), a PRD with wire-level API examples, a prototype reference implementation in Python + Node for streaming reconnection, telemetry plan (events + dashboards) to measure adoption and regressions, and a rollout plan including canaries for Dedicated/Private customers.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Maya Chen: Created ticket after consolidation of customer asks from Sales Q4 handoff and SE intake form (link in links). Initial triage: multiple enterprise accounts asking for Go and Java SDK parity and a few asking for resumable streaming in mobile networks.

2026-02-25 - Arjun Patel: Ran first-pass quantification: 14 unique customers requested language parity; top languages by ARR exposure: Java, Go, .NET. Added complexity estimate for each (rough). Marking as P1 because several customers are in active procurement cycles.

2026-03-02 - Eng lead (Priya Rao): Reviewed proposed streaming API patterns. Trade-off flagged: supporting resumable streams with KV-cache pinned to a host may force sticky routing on Dedicated—requires ENG-27234 changes. Added ENG dependency. Recommended an initial design that uses idempotent resume tokens and server-side ephemeral session objects to avoid long-lived sticky state.

2026-03-04 - Security (Leo Martins): Security review requested. Concern: token-refresh hooks across languages must avoid leaking long-lived secrets to client-side SDKs. Suggested adding guidance and sample patterns for on-prem KMS integration and server-side token minting. Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-03-07 - Design (Ana Gomez): Provided feedback on streaming ergonomics docs: prefer explicit ConnectionManager abstraction in SDKs with lifecycle hooks (onOpen, onResume, onError, onClose) and built-in exponential backoff + jitter. Also recommended single canonical spec document for generated clients to reduce language drift.

2026-03-09 - Arjun Patel: Updated prioritization matrix: created weighted scoring (customer ARR impact x3, implementation complexity x-1.5, support burden x-1, anonymized usage signal x2). Top candidates: (1) Java SDK parity for streaming + auth hooks, (2) Go SDK token-rotation patterns, (3) Reference resumable streaming prototype (Python + Node). Planning to open scoped PRD and prototype tasks next.

2026-03-10 - Maya Chen: Hit milestone: PRD draft posted and shared with stakeholders for review. Links below include draft PRD, prototype repo, and raw intake spreadsheet. Next: finalize acceptance criteria and schedule a 30-min cross-functional review (PM/ENG/SEC/DX).
